pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: Migration 0002 adds the column with a CHECK and DEFAULT 'normal'. test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' checks the existing rows are normal and that 'urgent' is rejected.
The 'AC-2' test checks the '— high' and '— low' labels and that normal items have none.
The 'AC-3' test checks high, low and normal filters in id order.
The 'AC-4' test checks '/' lists all items in id order.
The 'AC-5' test checks the exact nav markup for all four views.
The 'AC-6' test checks status 400 and no <li> for High, urgent, empty and __proto__.

The behaviour is implemented and tested, but commit 353b6b7 ('Follow-up edits') renamed the test and removed the 'AC-7' tag from its title. No test now names AC-7, and the spec has no 'verified by review' mark for it.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?priority=high'. The 'AC-8' test imports the file and checks it.

findings.what: The last commit, 353b6b7 'Follow-up edits', was made by a bot and strips 'AC-7:' from the test title. No test names AC-7 any more, so the item is unmet under the naming rule. The PR claims the tests cover AC-1 to AC-8, and that is no longer true.
findings.fix: Restore 'AC-7' in the test title. Drop the unexplained follow-up commit, or justify it.

findings.what: The README mentions the filter but not that high and low items are labelled, and not that other values answer 400.
findings.fix: Add one line about the labels and the 400 response.

lenses.note: The change follows the spec's go and its decisions: existing items are normal, and only high and low are labelled.
AC-7 is unnamed by any test after the last commit. The state table rows each have a test in the 'states' describe block.
The assertions check behaviour. I did not run the tests. The traffic-config shell test additions cover both the query string and the refused characters.
The README is only lightly updated.
The SQL is parameterized, the title is escaped, and an empty priority value correctly gives 400.
No injection found. The priority value is checked against a whitelist and bound as a parameter.
The change has only minimal server-rendered HTML and no UI or style files.
There is no browser session, so no UI flow was demonstrated.
The claim that the tests cover AC-1 to AC-8 is false after the last commit. The body also doesn't mention that commit.
